units.source_text: 且说朱雀院看了前斋宫对栉盒盖上的诗的答诗之后，对她的恋慕之情始终不离心怀。

en.t: After Suzaku-in read the former Ise priestess's reply to the poem on the lid of the comb box, his longing for her never left his heart.

units.source_text: 此时源氏内大臣前来参见了，与他闲话种种往事，顺便谈到了昔年斋宫下伊势时的情况。

en.t: Just then Genji, the Minister of the Interior, came to pay his respects, and as they chatted about various memories, the conversation turned to the time years before when the priestess went down to Ise.

units.source_text: 他们以前亦常谈起此事，今日重又提及。

en.t: They had often spoken of this before, and today they brought it up once again.

units.source_text: 但朱雀院并不明显表示自己曾经有心欲得此人。

en.t: But Suzaku-in did not openly show that he had once wished to make her his own.

units.source_text: 源氏内大臣也装作不知道他曾有此心，只是想试探他对此女的恋情深浅如何，从各方面讲了前斋宫的一些事。

en.t: Genji also pretended not to know that Suzaku-in had felt this way, and merely spoke about the former priestess from various angles in order to sound out the depth of his love for her.

units.source_text: 看他的神情，相思之心不浅，便对他深感同情。

en.t: Seeing his expression, Genji realized that his yearning was far from shallow, and felt deep sympathy for him.

units.source_text: 他想：“朱雀院如此念念不忘，想见此人一定生得异常美丽，但不知究竟如何。”

en.t: He thought, "If Suzaku-in cannot forget her like this, she must be extraordinarily beautiful, though I wonder what she is really like."

units.source_text: 他很想见她一面，然而这是办不到的，因此心中焦灼。

en.t: He very much wanted to see her once, but that was impossible, and so his heart grew restless with longing.

units.source_text: 原来这前斋宫生性异常稳重。

en.t: As it happened, this former priestess was by nature exceptionally composed.

units.source_text: 假如她略有轻佻举动，自然总有机会给人窥见颜面。

en.t: If she had behaved even a little frivolously, there would naturally have been chances for someone to catch a glimpse of her face.

units.source_text: 无如她年纪越是长大，性情越是端庄。

en.t: But the older she grew, the more dignified and restrained her character became.

units.source_text: 所以源氏内大臣只能在隔着帘帷相见之时想象她是个温恭贤良的淑女而已。

en.t: Therefore Genji, the Minister of the Interior, could only imagine, when meeting her through curtains and screens, that she was a gentle, courteous, and virtuous lady.
